L3-TXT5-21.text:
MOVEMENT RULE
Mode A - 3+1 late transfer: play digits 1-3 on the first string and digit 4 on the adjacent string.
Mode B - 1+3 early transfer: play digit 1 on the first string and digits 2-4 on the adjacent string.
Ascend through E/A, A/D, D/G, G/B, B/e. Descend through e/B, B/G, G/D, D/A, A/E.
The four-digit code order never changes.

WHY THIS IS LEVEL 3
Level 2 crossed after note 2. These modes cross after note 3 or note 1, so strict alternate picking produces different
inside- and outside-string transitions depending on whether the exercise begins with a downstroke or an upstroke.

PRACTICE RULE
Begin 8-12 BPM below your clean Level 2 tempo. Use one 12-code set and one mode per session.
Play each exercise ascending and descending, once beginning with a downstroke and once beginning with an upstroke.
First pass: lightly accent the first note after the crossing. Second pass: make all four notes equal in volume.
Rotate the existing straight-16th, triplet, and quintuplet groupings across sessions.
After three clean loops, add 2 BPM next time. After two errors or rising tension, reduce 4-6 BPM.
Advance when both modes for the set are clean on two separate days.

U-start: U D U D U D U D | U D U D U D U D
Do not restart the pick cycle at the scale turn or at the one-fret shift.

compiled-PDF2.text:
START HERE
Introduction & How to Use This Book
This collection brings the complete 105-level guitar curriculum into one continuous practice reference. It begins with finger
coordination, develops fretboard and harmonic control, and finishes with complete performances and original music. Treat each level
as a set of skills to demonstrate, rather than a race through pages.
A REPEATABLE PRACTICE LOOP
01
Read the level
Identify the module, key or position, rhythm and printed mastery
gate.
02
Isolate one challenge
Work on a manageable cell or transition at a controllable tempo.
03
Connect it to music
Restore the phrase, progression or full form. Listen for the target
skill.
04
Record and review
Capture evidence, name the weak boundary and choose the next
repair.
FINDING AND PRINTING MATERIAL
The contents on page 4 links to each section. Every section opener lists
its levels and book page ranges; PDF bookmarks reach all 105 levels.
Practice tools begin on page 1,772.
Print: US Letter, landscape, one PDF page per sheet side. Use actual size
(100%) when supported, or fit to the printable area if your printer clips
an edge. For duplex, use flip on short edge and test two pages first.
The complete book uses 1,777 single-sided sheets or 889 duplex sheets. Use
the contents to print section ranges for a binder. Pages are consecutive; no
blank divider backs are inserted.
Editorial navigation notes. The unnumbered finger-permutation PDF is indexed as Level 1. The older next-section notes at the end of Levels 29 and 48 are superseded: Level
30 begins major pentatonic, Level 49 begins chords and rhythm, and harmonic minor starts at Level 65. Source content and local page numbers remain; use the new bottom
footer for book page references.

L48-TXT1214-1246.text:
RECORD-AND-REVIEW RUBRIC - SCORE EACH 0, 1, OR 2
Form awareness: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Rhythmic space: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Chord targeting: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Bend and slide intonation: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Motif continuity: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Position movement: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Dynamic shape: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Recovery after an error: 0 absent / 1 inconsistent / 2 controlled.
Maximum 16. Section-completion standard: 13 or higher on two separate days, with no zero in form awareness,
chord targeting, or recovery.

PRACTICE PROGRESSION
1. Clap the call-and-response rhythms and count every rest.
2. Complete all five local pairs; exaggerate the phrase boundary.
3. Play all four seam conversations and verify every beat-one target.
4. Transform the seed motif in seven ways without changing tempo.
5. Perform sparse, medium, and dense passes at one BPM.
6. Perform the three dynamic-shape exercises without changing subdivision.
7. Learn each model chorus in four-bar blocks, then play all twelve bars.
8. Replace one response bar at a time while preserving the written calls.
9. Practice tonic closes and E7 re-entries until bar 12 has a clear purpose.
10. Record the three-chorus capstone, score it, repair one category, and record again.

MASTERY GATE - SECTION V COMPLETE
Perform all five local pairs and four seam conversations; transform one motif in seven ways; preserve targets
through sparse, medium, and dense passes; play all three model choruses; execute both a tonic ending and a
functional turnaround; recover from a deliberate wrong note without stopping; record three connected choruses
on two separate days; make the A7-D7-E7 form audible without accompaniment; and score at least 13/16.

NEXT SECTION
Section VI begins harmonic minor. Natural minor degree b7 is raised to 7, creating the minor-key dominant,
the augmented-second interval between b6 and 7, and a new set of chord-tone and phrasing demands.

Low E string: R, R+2               Fingers 2,4

D string:     R-1, R+1, R+2        Fingers 1,3,4

ROLLING THREE-NOTE SEQUENCE
UP:   1-2-3 | 2-3-4 | 3-4-5 | 4-5-6 | 5-6-7 | 6-7-8 | 7-8-9 | 8-9-10 | 9-10-11 | 10-11-12 | 11-12-13 | 12-13-14 | 13-14-15
DOWN: 15-14-13 | 14-13-12 | 13-12-11 | 12-11-10 | 11-10-9 | 10-9-8 | 9-8-7 | 8-7-6 | 7-6-5 | 6-5-4 | 5-4-3 | 4-3-2 | 3-2-1
Each new triplet starts one scale position farther along. The line moves forward three notes, then rolls
back one position to begin the next group. Do not pause or reset at a triplet boundary, string crossing,
the middle-octave root, the high-root turn, or the one-fret relocation.

CELL AND PICKING RULE
The complete cell contains 26 triplets and 78 notes: 13 ascending groups and 13 descending groups.
The last note of 13-14-15 is followed immediately by the first note of 15-14-13, so the high root is
played twice at the turn. Because 78 is even, the next key begins with the same pick orientation.
D-start groups: D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U ... through all 26 groups.
U-start groups: U-D-U | D-U-D | U-D-U | D-U-D ... through all 26 groups.
Never restart the pick cycle at a new group, string crossing, octave, scale turn, or one-fret shift.

Do not spend the entire block chasing one uncertain extension.

A successful recovery is worth more than preserving a difficult but failing original part.

Minute
Task

The work must sound authored: identity, form, development, return, and ending.

L105-PDF28.text:
Final Examination - Block 8: Reflection and Final Declaration
Question
Answer in one sentence
What is your strongest domain?
What still needs specialization?
Which fallback saved the most performances?
Which technique do you now use less because you understand it better?
What is the next repertoire/composition goal?
What specialization track will you pursue, if any?
The core curriculum ends with self-directed musicianship. Future study should be chosen by musical goal, not by an arbitrary next level number.
